clue.text: Does as replacement for port

indicators.note: a replacement puts things in new places, so the letters of the two opening words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone substitutes a verb form for a harbour, as if editing a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' tells you to rearrange DOES and AS; 'for' is only a link to the definition 'port', the Black Sea city.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea seaport in Ukraine.

clue.text: Horace lacks aspiration, we hear to join radical support for Florentine flag

indicators.note: we hear means the dropped-aitch name is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the name Horace said without its H sound, as 'Orace
radical means of the root, and a root supports a plant

explanation.surface: A man called Horace drops his aitches while backing an Italian banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks aspiration' drops the H; flag here is the iris plant, and the Florentine iris gives orris root, used in perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris root is the fragrant dried rhizome of the Florentine iris, a flag being another name for an iris.

clue.text: Where to find church choir in London

definitions.text: Where to find church choir in London

parts.words: Where to find church choir in London
parts.note: the choir of a church lies at its eastern end, and the same phrase names a district of London

explanation.surface: A visitor asks where a church choir might be found in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Churches are oriented with the choir and altar at the east; the East End is the area of London east of the City.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel and choir of a church sit at the eastern end, also the name of a London district.

clue.text: Bardolph's nose described as red-hot poker

explanation.surface: A drinker's glowing nose is compared to a heated iron.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Henry IV, Falstaff calls Bardolph's red nose a salamander; the word also means a poker heated red-hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff mocks his crony's fiery nose with the name of a fire-dwelling creature, which is also a heated iron.

clue.text: This cloth to use for waterproof coat?

definitions.text: This cloth to use for waterproof coat?

parts.words: This cloth to use for waterproof coat?
parts.note: the clue asks for the name of a glazed, oil-treated fabric used to keep the rain out, named after a country's people

explanation.surface: A tailor wonders which fabric would make a rainproof coat.
explanation.walkthrough: American cloth is an old name for a glazed, enamelled oilcloth used for table covers and waterproofs.
explanation.definitionFit: American cloth was a shiny waterproofed fabric, so the nationality adjective names the material.

clue.text: So brilliant a flare amusing me perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words amusing me might be arranged in some other way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dazzling firework display entertains the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AMUSING ME.
explanation.definitionFit: This metal burns with an intensely bright white light, used in flares and early photography.

clue.text: Are you, so to speak, at home in such a tumbledown place?

indicators.note: so to speak means the two words are spoken and represented by the letters they sound like

parts.note: the words sound like the letters R and U
at home means in

explanation.surface: Someone asks if you live in a crumbling house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' turns 'Are you' into the letters R and U, as in text speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruin is a building that has collapsed or decayed.

clue.text: Goldsmith's nomination is welcome in Italy

definitions.text: Goldsmith's nomination is welcome in Italy

parts.words: Goldsmith's nomination is welcome in Italy
parts.note: the Renaissance goldsmith's first name, Benvenuto, is the Italian for welcome

explanation.surface: An award for a goldsmith is well received by Italians.
explanation.walkthrough: Benvenuto Cellini, Florentine goldsmith and sculptor: his given name means 'welcome' in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was the celebrated sixteenth-century Florentine goldsmith whose first name means welcome.

clue.text: Homeric bird?

parts.note: a tropical tern named for nodding, and Homer proverbially nods, so a nodding bird is Homeric

explanation.surface: A bird out of Homer's epics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even Homer nods' means great minds slip; the noddy is a tern, so a nodding bird is Homeric.
explanation.definitionFit: The noddy is a tropical tern whose name suggests nodding, which Homer famously does.

clue.text: Attend police course

explanation.surface: Someone goes on a training course for officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attend' is read as 'be at', run together.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present somewhere is to be at it, and a constable's regular patrol route is his beat.

clue.text: Decision to disperse

explanation.surface: A choice is made to break up a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm determination is a resolve, and to resolve also means to break up or dissolve into parts.

clue.text: Broiled, poor girl, having been in the van

indicators.note: poor suggests the word girl is in bad shape and so has its letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
to be in the van is to be at the front, leading, so this gives led

explanation.surface: A girl left in a hot van has been cooked like meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges GIRL to GRIL; 'in the van' means at the front, the vanguard, so having been there is LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Broiling is the American word for cooking under direct heat, the same as grilling.

clue.text: She has a relatively cruel reputation

definitions.text: She has a relatively cruel reputation

parts.words: She has a relatively cruel reputation
parts.note: relatively is read as 'as a relative': a woman related by marriage who is cruel in fairy tales

explanation.surface: A woman is known for being somewhat unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' seems to mean 'fairly', but it points to a family relation: the wicked one of Cinderella and Snow White.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's later wife is the stock villain of fairy tales, notorious for cruelty.

clue.text: Ruth's expression of regret

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth says she is sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a name, but ruth is an old word for compassion; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic noun for compassion, and 'what a shame!' is the same exclamation of regret.

clue.text: Photogenic hunting expert?

parts.note: read as someone skilled at searching or looking, it describes an attractive person

explanation.surface: A hunter who looks good in pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunting expert might be good at looking for things; an attractive person is a good-looker.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive person who photographs well is called a good-looker.

clue.text: It could be first spoken without much noise

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for spoken goes around the word for noise

parts.note: spoken means oral, said rather than written
a din is a lot of noise

explanation.surface: Something might come top if said quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'outside', so ORAL wraps DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: First, second and third are numbers giving position in a sequence, the class of word in question.

clue.text: As man of property, poet arranged new enclosure

indicators.note: enclosure means the poet's name goes around the rearranged word

parts.note: Walter Savage Landor was an English poet

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of new are put in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rich man's verse-writing friend sets up a new fence.
explanation.walkthrough: Landor (Walter Savage Landor) is a crossword poet; 'arranged' turns NEW into WNE, and 'enclosure' puts it inside LANDOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owns estates or land is a man of property.

clue.text: Having teeth like a kind of key?

definitions.text: Having teeth like a kind of key?

parts.words: Having teeth like a kind of key?
parts.note: teeth and piano keys were both once made of elephant tusk, so the adjective describes white, tusk-like teeth

explanation.surface: Someone's teeth are being compared with a key cut for a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: The key is a piano key, traditionally faced with tusk; the surface suggests a door key with teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were faced with elephant tusk, so teeth resembling them are white and tusk-like.

clue.text: Made out record before bird died

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
an erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: Someone saw a record played before a bird died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply puts DISC first; ERNE is a crossword sea eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something out is to perceive or detect it.

clue.text: Can bird appear in the Abbey?

parts.note: a can is a tin
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A question of whether a bird is able to show up in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, a tin. Tintern Abbey is a ruined abbey in the Wye valley, Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintern is the Welsh village whose ruined Cistercian monastery was made famous by Wordsworth's poem.

clue.text: It's not so good to be drunk in town of Gwent

definitions.text: It's not so good to be drunk

explanation.surface: A remark that it is unwise to get drunk in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Port wine improves with age, so a young one is not so good to drink; Newport is a town in Gwent, south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Young fortified wine is inferior to aged, and Newport is the main town of Gwent in Wales.

clue.text: Dividing lines for rigid old lawmen

explanation.surface: Lines are drawn to separate strict old-fashioned law enforcers.
explanation.walkthrough: The laws of the Medes and Persians were proverbially unalterable; a Median is a Mede, a person of ancient Media.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry such lines run from a vertex to the middle of the opposite side, and people of ancient Media were famous for unchangeable laws.

clue.text: Use soda with pie, otherwise it becomes fatty

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters are set out in another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that eating pie with soda makes you fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges SODA and PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fat store.

clue.text: Bird's cry heard in the grounds during game season

indicators.note: heard means the word for the cry is listened to rather than read, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: the cry from football spectators at an illegal tackle is 'Foul!'

explanation.surface: A bird's call rings out over the sports ground while matches are being played.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue sets the scene: the cry is the one heard at sports grounds during the football season. 'Bird's' is 'bird is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowl is a general word for birds, especially domestic or game birds.

clue.text: Young horse caught inside by this length of lens

indicators.note: inside means the abbreviation goes in the middle of the horse word

parts.note: a foal is a young horse
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A foal trapped inside is photographed with a particular lens.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer replaces 'this' in 'this length of lens', giving focal length.
explanation.definitionFit: Focal length is the distance from a lens to its point of focus.

clue.text: Cartoonist's side-view kept out of the limelight

parts.note: David Low was a famous political cartoonist for the London Evening Standard
a profile is a view from the side

explanation.surface: A caricaturist's sketch from the side was hidden from the public.
explanation.walkthrough: Low is a crossword favourite: Sir David Low, creator of Colonel Blimp.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a low profile means avoiding attention and publicity.

clue.text: Victoria's cushy job

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria has an easy position.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a popular English variety of this fruit; a cushy job is a plum one. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is a well-known variety of the fruit, and a highly desirable post is called a plum.

clue.text: Look at nobleman as equal

explanation.surface: Treating an aristocrat as an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look closely, a peer is a lord, and a peer is also one's equal.

clue.text: What the weather may do in the immediate vicinity

explanation.surface: A forecast remark about the weather nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad weather closes in when it surrounds and darkens, and something close in is very near at hand.

clue.text: This god of the Athenians declared to them by St Paul

definitions.text: This god of the Athenians declared to them by St Paul

parts.words: This god of the Athenians declared to them by St Paul
parts.note: in Acts 17 Paul finds an Athenian altar inscribed to a nameless god and preaches that god to them

explanation.surface: A reference to Paul's sermon on the Areopagus in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: Acts 17:23: 'To the Unknown God. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.'
explanation.definitionFit: The altar was dedicated to a deity whose identity the Athenians did not know.

clue.text: Such was Johnson's club in reality, right — but wrong

indicators.note: wrong means the letters have been put in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Claims that Samuel Johnson's club was really something are shown to be false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges REALITY plus R. Samuel Johnson's dining club of writers and artists was called The Literary Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Johnson founded a famous society of writers in 1764, known simply as The Club or by this bookish adjective.

clue.text: Fox was Society man originally

parts.note: George Fox founded the Religious Society of ..., the Quakers, so he was the first member of that society

explanation.surface: A fox is said to have started out as a society gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Fox is George Fox, founder of the Quakers, whose members are called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Society of Friends is a Quaker, and George Fox was the first.
